chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: Why he left Duke; working on his own
summary: He couldn't wait for the band's club job, and found his own work including Le Downbeat.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But you being a person who had been really "a leader," for you to stay in a situation like that wasn't really you, because you were like a leader.
Yeah. Well, it wasn't paying me to stay in that band, you know. That's my thing. That's what I had to compete with, how much money I was taking in with Duke or
with anybody. When I could work on my own... I could always work or get a gig in Birdland or 54th Street and Eighth Avenue...
Was that the name of the club?
Yeah, Le Downbeat. That was in the early Fifties, though. That only lasted for a few years.
Yeah, they didn't last too long.
No. It was a nice club, though.
Yeah, it was nice. I remember, I worked there a couple of times. Brew and I, too... And Allan Eager, that's right; Allan Eager worked there a little bit.
